Coefficient Derivatives of a Quadratic Penalty

Source: R/quadratic_penalty.R
penalty_gradient.QuadraticPenalty.Rd

penalty_gradient() returns \(\lambda D'PD\beta\) and penalty_hessian() returns \(\lambda D'PD\). Both read the cached \(D'PD\), so neither touches the map at call time, and the Hessian does not depend on \(\beta\) at all, the value being a quadratic form.

Arguments

pen

A QuadraticPenalty() object.

beta

A numeric vector of length pen@n_coef.

theta

A list holding lambda.

...

Unused, and accepted so that the signature matches the generic's.

Value

penalty_gradient() a numeric vector of length pen@n_coef; penalty_hessian() a symmetric matrix of that side, a base matrix for an ordinary penalty and a dgCMatrix when the penalty was built with blocks > 1.

Details

Because the Hessian is constant, the gradient is exactly the Hessian applied to the coefficients, and a Newton step on this penalty alone reaches the minimum in one iteration from anywhere.

See also

penalty_value.QuadraticPenalty() for the quantity differentiated, penalty_grad_theta.QuadraticPenalty() for the hyperparameter derivatives.

Examples

pen <- quadratic_penalty(crossprod(diff(diag(4))))
b <- c(1, -0.5, 0.2, 2)

# The gradient is the constant Hessian applied to the coefficients.
all.equal(penalty_gradient(pen, b, list(lambda = 3)),
          drop(penalty_hessian(pen, b, list(lambda = 3)) %*% b))
#> [1] TRUE

# The Hessian does not move with beta.
all.equal(penalty_hessian(pen, b, list(lambda = 3)),
          penalty_hessian(pen, 0 * b, list(lambda = 3)))
#> [1] TRUE
